question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{22-7x}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=22-7x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-7.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-7) \\  & =-\frac{7}{2\sqrt{22-7x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(-\frac{7}{2\sqrt{22-7x}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =\frac{-7}{2\sqrt{22-7(-2)}} \\  & =\frac{-7}{2\sqrt{36}} \\  & =-\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-3x+42}+3{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{-3x+42}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-3x+42.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-3) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{-3x+42}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{-3x+42}}+9x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & =-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{-3(2)+42}}+9(2)^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}+36 \\  & =\frac{143}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
